quote: “Enlightenment is man’s emergence from his self-incurred immaturity.”
source: Immanuel Kant, An Answer to the Question: What is Enlightenment?, opening sentence (trans. H. B. Nisbet, 1970)

evidence.where: James Schmidt’s Persistent Enlightenment survey of nine translations, quoting the Nisbet rendering from Reiss (ed.), Kant: Political Writings, Cambridge, 1970; the volume itself was not opened, page 54 is the standard placement
evidence.edition: Kant: Political Writings, ed. Hans Reiss, trans. H. B. Nisbet, Cambridge University Press, 1970, p. 54

reason: The wording is Nisbet’s exactly, distinguished from Beck (tutelage), Humphrey (self-imposed) and Gregor (minority) in a scholarly comparison. Not shipped, not at cap, not banned.
